title: They Donated From Abroad to Build the Ram Temple. Eight Men Were Stealing the Money.
excerpt: A court in Ayodhya has detained eight men — including banking staff — over the systematic embezzlement of devotee donations at India's most politically charged temple. The racket ran for years.
body:
Devotees across India and the global diaspora who emptied their wallets — and in many cases wired money from abroad — to help build the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya are now confronting an unsettling question: where exactly did their offerings end up?

An Indian court on Monday detained eight men in connection with the alleged systematic embezzlement of donations at the grand temple dedicated to Lord Ram, the latest and most consequential step in a scandal that has embarrassed Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party, the political movement most closely identified with the temple's construction.

## What Happened

The arrests follow an FIR registered on June 25 at the Ram Janmabhoomi Police Station, based on a complaint by Krishanmohan, a member of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust — the body charged with managing the temple and its finances. A Special Investigation Team appointed by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath submitted a preliminary report on June 27 that flagged multiple irregularities in how cash and valuables donated by visiting devotees were collected, counted, and deposited.

The eight arrested include Tinnu Yadav, the former driver of the Trust's ex-general secretary Champat Rai; Subhash Srivastava, a retired SBI employee who oversaw cash counting at the Pilgrim Facility Centre; and six outsourced workers responsible for tallying donations. Police recovered ₹79.85 lakh (~$85,000) from seven of the accused.


![Lord Ram — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/45/Lord_Rama_with_arrows.jpg)



> **"The petition cited what it called "institutional denial" by Trust officials who dismissed early media reports as rumours."**



Investigators say the operation was sophisticated. According to police sources, cash bundles were stored in bathrooms to evade detection, moved out of the temple premises at night, and diverted to personal accounts. The racket is believed to have operated for two to three years.

## The SBI Connection

The involvement of banking staff has turned a temple scandal into something more complex. Two SBI employees at the Naya Ghat branch — which maintains the Trust's main account — are under scrutiny. Both supervised the outsourced counting staff. Police visited the branch on Monday to question the branch manager and record statements.

NDTV reported that SBI had recommended removing the counting staff about three months ago after detecting suspected irregularities, but certain Trust officials opposed the move. That detail may sharpen questions about whether the misappropriation could have been stopped earlier.

The SIT's preliminary report also flagged the absence of mandatory safeguards that should have been in place: CCTV footage was not consistently preserved, security guards were not deployed during the counting process, and standard operating procedures for handling high-value donations were routinely violated. Investigators have since replaced all personnel previously responsible for managing the donation process and recommended a complete overhaul of the system.


![Prime Minister Narendra Modi — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/5f/The_official_portrait_of_Shri_Narendra_Modi%2C_the_Prime_Minister_of_the_Republic_of_India.jpg)


Police conducted coordinated searches at the residences of all eight suspects on Sunday, recovering jewellery and documents linked to the investigation. Authorities said further searches are planned at suspects' hometowns outside Ayodhya.

## Political Fallout

The Ram Mandir is not just a temple — it is the most potent symbol of the BJP's political identity. Modi personally consecrated it in January 2024 in a ceremony broadcast to millions worldwide. The embezzlement scandal hands the opposition a rare opening.

Former UP Chief Minister Akhilesh Yadav has demanded accountability. Ayodhya MP Awadhesh Prasad has called for a court-monitored investigation and the removal of Trust members until the inquiry concludes. Even some BJP leaders have called for clarity.

A PIL filed in the Allahabad High Court seeks a CBI probe and a CAG forensic audit of the Trust's accounts. The petition cited what it called "institutional denial" by Trust officials who dismissed early media reports as rumours.

## Why the Diaspora Should Care

The Ram Mandir was funded primarily by donations — many from NRIs who contributed through organised campaigns across the United States, Canada, the UK, and the Gulf. For diaspora donors who gave to what they considered a civilisational project, the alleged theft raises pointed questions about the Trust's governance, the absence of independent auditing, and whether the structures set up to manage one of the most symbolically important projects in modern India are adequate.

The SIT's final report, expected within 15 days, will determine how far the investigation reaches. But the damage to public trust has already begun.
